title: The CLI alone teaches the toolkit (no agent, no skill installed)
expectation: An agent that has only the binary — no skill installed, no repository, no network — must be able to find the guidance from the CLI alone: `pina --help` advertises the skill, `pina docs` cross-references it, `pina skill` lists the topics, `pina skill read` serves the same documents the npm package ships, and `pina skill install` writes a usable tree that it refuses to clobber. These checks are deterministic; the facts they grep for are the ones the evaluations showed agents actually need.

checks.why: Discovery has to start at `pina --help`, the first thing the skill itself tells an agent to inspect.
An agent that found the docs surface first must be pointed at the skill surface.
The listing is the index an agent scans before choosing what to read.
The entrypoint must carry the routing table and the migration loop, byte for byte as shipped.

expectOutput: relative to the version envelope header
checks.why: These are exactly the facts the evaluations showed agents need: the transition ABI, the disambiguation flags, the envelope gate, the document version, and the layout drift gate.
Agents parse the document itself; terminal rendering would corrupt frontmatter and code blocks.

checks.command: rm -rf .work-install && pina skill install --dir .work-install/pina && python3 -c "import os; assert os.path.exists('.work-install/pina/references/migrations.md'); assert open('.work-install/pina/SKILL.md').read().startswith('---')"
checks.why: An install must produce the whole skill tree with the entrypoint intact.
Replacing a curated skill is not a side effect an install may have without --force.
The explicit override must exist and work.
A scripting agent relies on exit status, not prose, to notice a misspelled topic.
